This Petition, Coming On For Admission, This Day,
The Court Made The Following:
 Order

1. This petition is presented challenging the registration of an FIR for the offenses punishable under Section 420 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 (hereinafter for brevity referred to as "the IPC") against the petitioner.

2. In the complaint dated 25.03.2017, the second respondent contended that he had lent a sum of Rs.20,00,000/- (Rupees twenty lakhs) to the petitioner and for repayment of the said amount the petitioner had issued a cheque dated 15.12.2016 for a sum Rs.20,00,000/- (Rupees twenty lakhs)
and when said cheque was presented, the same was returned with an endorsement "Funds Insufficient" "Drawer's Signature incomplete/illegible/Differs/Required" and "Alteration requires drawer's authentication".

Alleging that there was a dishonest intention on the part of the petitioner to deceive him, the complaint was lodged and as stated NC: 2024:KHC:20986 above, the police registered an FIR for an offence under section 420 of the IPC.

3. Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that, as a matter of fact, the second respondent had initiated proceedings for commission of an offence punishable under Section 138 of the Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881 (hereinafter for brevity referred to as the "N.I.Ac") and this was the very same cheque in C.C.No.53395/2017 and said proceedings ended in an acquittal in favour of the petitioner.

Learned counsel for the petitioner places on record a copy of the judgment passed C.C.No.53395/2017 and also submits that an appeal filed against said order in Crl.A.No.1244/2022 has also been dismissed for non- prosecution.
4. In light of the fact that this was the very same complaint the second respondent had initiated proceedings under Section 138 of the N.I.Act and was unsuccessful in establishing the liability of the petitioner, in my view, no useful purpose would be served by permitting the NC: 2024:KHC:20986 prosecution for offences punishable under Section 420 of the IPC to continue.
Consequently, the proceedings initiated by the second respondent against the petitioner which are impugned in this petition shall stand quashed.
5. The Criminal Petition is accordingly allowed.
